record.paper_title: SOFT PHYSICS AND INTERMITTENCY : OPEN QUESTION(S) in KRAKOW
record.original_question: When factorial analyses in different phase-space dimensions reveal different dynamical excitations, how should lower-dimensional intermittency be interpreted if Bose-Einstein correlations dominate most three-dimensional studies, and how should Ochs-Wosiek moments-over-moments scaling in one- and two-dimensional NA22 studies be explained?

evidence.quote: 2. The "Wall and Tower" problem. As is clear, e.g. in the analysis of ref.[14], the factorial analysis in different dimension can reveal different types of dynamical excitations.

If then, Bose-Einstein correlations dominate in most cases the 3-dimensional studies, what about lower dimensionalities? In particular how to interpret the Ochs-Wosiek scaling (moments over moments) in 1- and 2-dimensional NA22 studies[10]?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. In multiparticle production experiments one studies scaled factorial moments
   F_q(δ) = ⟨ n(n−1)···(n−q+1) ⟩ / ⟨ n ⟩^q
of charged-particle multiplicities n in cells of size δ obtained by partitioning a D-dimensional phase-space region (D = 1, 2, 3, with variables such as rapidity, azimuthal angle, and transverse momentum). "Intermittency" denotes a power-law growth F_q(δ) ∝ δ^{−φ_q} as δ → 0. The Ochs–Wosiek relation is the empirical "moments-over-moments" scaling
   ln F_q(δ) = c_q · ln F_2(δ) + d_q,
observed (in particular in the NA22 π⁺p and K⁺p data at √s = 22 GeV) in one- and two-dimensional analyses, with slope ratios c_q that depend on the dimensionality D in which the moments are computed.

It is widely accepted that in three-dimensional phase space the intermittency signal is dominated by Bose–Einstein correlations between identical bosons (the two-particle correlator C_2(Q) being well described by a function of the four-momentum difference Q only in 3D).

Problem. Provide a dynamical interpretation of the lower-dimensional (D = 1 and D = 2) intermittency signal that is consistent with Bose–Einstein correlations being the dominant source of the three-dimensional signal. Concretely:

(a) Identify the physical mechanism(s) producing the observed power-law growth of F_q(δ) when phase space is projected onto one or two dimensions, given that the genuine identical-particle Bose–Einstein correlation acts in the full three-dimensional Q-space and is partially washed out under projection.

(b) Derive, within this mechanism, the dependence of the Ochs–Wosiek slope ratios c_q = φ_q/φ_2 on the dimension D, and reproduce quantitatively the c_q values observed in the one- and two-dimensional NA22 factorial-moment analyses.

(c) Explain why factorial-moment analyses performed in different phase-space dimensions can reveal apparently different dynamical excitations (the "wall-and-tower" effect), and specify under what conditions lower-dimensional intermittency cannot be reduced to a kinematic projection of a purely three-dimensional Bose–Einstein dynamics.
artifact.category_tag: Intermittency and Bose-Einstein correlations in multiparticle production
artifact.status_search_result: Searches indicate continued analysis by NA22 and theoretical work attributing 3D intermittency largely to Bose–Einstein correlations, while lower-dimensional Ochs–Wosiek scaling has been fitted phenomenologically (e.g., by Lévy stable laws with index μ≈1.6). No definitive, generally accepted dynamical derivation reconciling the 1D/2D Ochs–Wosiek scaling with a Bose–Einstein-dominated 3D picture was located, so the question appears to remain unresolved at the level of a first-principles explanation.

status_evidence.title: New NA22 Results on Correlations
status_evidence.snippet: Recent NA22 results on invariant-mass and Q²-dependence of two- and three-particle factorial cumulants are discussed in relation to earlier intermittency studies.
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent NA22 analyses continued to address the connection between intermittency and Bose–Einstein correlations without a fully settled interpretation.

status_evidence.title: Factorial moments and correlations in meson-nucleus interactions at 250 GeV/c
status_evidence.snippet: Rise of factorial moments and cumulants with decreasing phase-space volume is stronger in 3D than in lower dimensions; order dependence better described by a Lévy stable law with μ≈1.6.
status_evidence.claim: Lower-dimensional Ochs–Wosiek scaling is described phenomenologically rather than derived from a unique dynamical mechanism.

status_evidence.title: Bose-Einstein source of intermittency in hadronic interactions
status_evidence.snippet: Multiparticle Bose-Einstein correlations are considered the source of intermittency in high energy hadronic collisions.
status_evidence.claim: BE correlations are widely viewed as the dominant 3D source, leaving the lower-dimensional interpretation a separate open issue.
